name: Energy & AI Power
tagline: AI data centres need electricity on a scale not seen in decades. This theme follows the money along the power chain — fuel (uranium, natural gas, oil), generation (utilities, nuclear), the grid that carries it, and the clean-energy build-out. Same story, very different risks: commodity-price bets, regulated utilities, fee-earning pipelines and policy-driven clean energy.
universe_note: Six segments: Nuclear & uranium (URA, URNM, URNJ, NLR, NUKZ), Power & grid (GRID, ELFY), Utilities (VPU), Gas & midstream pipelines (AMLP, ENFR), Oil & gas (XOP; XLE as yardstick) and Clean energy (ICLN). Filter by segment above the table. The full-universe list below also carries newer AI-power funds, London-listed UCITS versions and clearly-tagged leveraged products.
key_tensions: Commodity price vs toll road: producers and miners (XOP, URNM, URA) swing with oil, gas and uranium prices; pipelines (AMLP, ENFR) earn fees on volumes — steadier and income-heavy, but capped upside.
AI-power story vs regulated returns: utilities sell the electricity, but regulators cap their profits — great demand doesn't automatically mean great returns for VPU-type funds.
Uranium spot-price dependence: nuclear funds live and die on a volatile commodity with a brutal boom-bust history; Cameco alone is ~20%+ of URA/URNM.
Clean energy has been a value trap: rate- and subsidy-sensitive (ICLN fell for years after 2021) — the AI-power tailwind hasn't removed the policy risk.
Grid is the picks-and-shovels play: transformers, cables, switchgear (GRID, ELFY) benefit whichever fuel wins — but many holdings are industrials you may already own.
Single-country / geopolitical risk: uranium supply (Kazakhstan, Canada), LNG export policy and oil (OPEC) all add headline risk outside the companies' control.
MLP tax drag: AMLP holds partnerships but is taxed as a corporation (no K-1 for you, but a tax drag inside the fund that shows up as weaker total return).
benchmark_note: XLE (broad US oil & gas, ~0.08%) is the yardstick, NOT an AI-power fund: it shows what cheap, diversified, dividend-paying energy delivered, so you can judge whether each segment's extra risk or fee was rewarded.
